evidence_used: Object image showing a whole avocado with a textured, pebbled skin surface.
Gecko gripper embodiment description specifying rigid fingers, mushroom-tipped dry-adhesive pads, and sensitivity to surface roughness and lack of flatness.
calculation_summary: Estimated required force based on visual surface texture (pebbled/rough skin) which degrades dry-adhesive performance, requiring higher normal force to maintain frictional and mechanical grip against the rigid gecko pads under gravity and object mass constraints.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: No authoritative mass or friction coefficient measurements were provided.
Visual assessment of surface curvature and texture is approximate.
Object is assumed to be grasped along its natural flanks despite curved geometry.
reasoning_trace: The query image displays an avocado, which has a naturally pebbled, bumpy, and non-flat skin. The gecko gripper relies heavily on clean, flat, smooth surfaces to maximize van der Waals contact with its mushroom-tipped dry adhesive pads. Because the avocado's surface is textured and curved rather than flat and smooth, gecko adhesion performance is significantly degraded. Consequently, the gripper must rely more heavily on standard frictional support provided by normal force application. To compensate for reduced adhesion and securely lift the object without slipping, a moderately high stationary-finger normal force of 5.5 N is estimated.
